lines: He's 19.{nineteen.} He already sold one AI startup. And now he's raised $10M{ten million dollars} for the next one.
I'm the AI Khabari, and this kid is not slowing down.
Meet Zach Yadegari. As a teen, he co-founded Cal AI, an app that counts calories from a photo of your food.
It reportedly made over $30M{thirty million dollars} a year. In March, MyFitnessPal bought it.
Most people would take a break. Zach left in June and started again.
His new startup is called Persona. It's an AI assistant you just text, like a friend.
Ask a normal chatbot to book you a ride, and it tells you how. Ask Persona, and it actually books it. Food, rides, travel, even your emails.
Next up, a $179{one hundred seventy nine dollar} wristband, coming in December.
But here's the catch. To stay free, Persona will mix sponsored picks into its shopping suggestions.
So your new assistant might also be a salesman.
Would you let an AI with ads run your errands? Tell me below, and send this to a friend who's still waiting to start.
